title: Quarterly plan: graceful degradation & priority fanout for dedicated pools
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Objective: build a compact, testable quarterly roadmap that reduces customer-visible failures when Dedicated pools are constrained by implementing graceful degradation policies and a priority-based fanout routing layer. This ticket captures the scope, success metrics, experiments, and rollout cadence for Q1/Q2 initiatives that stop over-provision reaction cycles and keep high-value traffic served within SLOs.

Why now: repeated small-scale contention incidents in dedicated pools have exposed brittle fallback behavior and noisy, manual escalations. Instead of adding headroom we can improve survivability and predictability through software: graded fallbacks, traffic prioritization, fast-path vs cost-path routing, and canary rehearsals.

Deliverables:
- Policy model spec (priority classes, degradation actions, timeouts) and mapping to customer tiers.
- Small state machine implementation in routing layer with unit tests and integration tests.
- 3 automated experiments (latency-preserving fallback, token-budgeted degradation, regional fanout test).
- Canary runbook and rehearsal schedule for SRE/operator teams.
- Dashboard tiles and alert rules that show degradation actions and customer impact.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Reduce P99 availability incidents caused by pool exhaustion by 40% vs baseline (last 90 days).
- Mean time to automatic fallback (detection -> policy action) < 30s.
- Less than 5% increase in average token cost for critical customers due to prioritized reroutes.
- Complete 3 canary rehearsals with no manual rollback during the quarter.

Scope exclusions: this ticket focuses on control-plane policy, routing, and observability. It excludes large infra purchases, long-running capacity buys, and private deployment-specific RBAC changes (these will be tracked separately).
